title: Surface Area of a Right Circular Cone
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Show that revolving the line segment y = (r/h) x from x = 0 to x = h about the x-axis yields the lateral surface area of a cone S = pi r sqrt(r^2 + h^2).

steps.title: Compute Derivative and ds
steps.explanation: Constant slope yields constant arc length factor.

steps.title: Set Up Integral
steps.mathExpression: S = 2\pi \int_0^h \left(\frac{r}{h} x\right) \frac{\sqrt{r^2 + h^2}}{h} dx = \frac{2\pi r \sqrt{r^2 + h^2}}{h^2} \int_0^h x \, dx

steps.title: Evaluate Definite Integral
steps.why: Classical lateral cone surface area formula.
